content.text: Analysis of the change: **build_index.py (only executable code):** - Entry points: CLI args `path` and `--title`. Local build tool, not a network service. - Sinks reviewed: - `open(out, "w")` writes to `os.path.join(root, "index.html")` — root is a CLI-supplied directory, no traversal since it's the write target itself, and `basename()` is used to reduce file references to their basename before HTML embedding. - No shell/exec/subprocess/eval. - HTML rendering uses f-strings, but every dynamic value (`title`, `L["title"]`, `d["file"]`) passes through `esc()` which is `html.escape(x, quote=True)`. - Title extraction from ``/`<h1>` in scanned HTML files: extracted, HTML-unescaped, but re-escaped via `esc(title)` on output. Safe. - `derive_title()` reads local PROGRESS.md/README.md; content re-escaped when rendered. - `parse()` uses `os.path.basename()` before regex — no path traversal possible. - No SSRF, no deserialization, no dynamic code loading. **HTML drill/lesson files (client-side JS):** - All quiz content is a static in-file `BANK` array — not attacker-controlled. - User input: only `textarea` value (`s.typed`), used exclusively as input to `String.indexOf()` for local keyword matching — not rendered. - Rendering paths that use `innerHTML`: - `renderCheck`: builds HTML but wraps concept labels in `esc(h.c.label)` (labels are from static BANK). - `renderModel`: `m.innerHTML = "<strong>Model answer.</strong> " + esc(q.model)` — escaped, and `q.model` is static. - Results table `esc(CHANNELS[q.ch])` and `esc(q.q.slice(...))` — escaped, static. - All option text uses `li.textContent = opt.t` — safe. - The custom `esc()` helper (`div.textContent = s; return d.innerHTML`) is a standard, correct HTML-escape idiom. - Lesson quiz options use `dataset.why` written back via `textContent` — safe. **index.html:** static output from build_index.py, same escaping properties. No entry points reach a dangerous sink without appropriate encoding. No path traversal, no XSS, no shell injection, no SSRF, no unsafe deserialization.
